steps: Any moving object has kinetic energy.

items.prompt: Name the two factors kinetic energy depends on.

steps: Both the mass and speed affect kinetic energy.

items.prompt: Two objects move at the same speed; one has more mass. Which has more kinetic energy?

steps: More mass means more kinetic energy at the same speed.

items.prompt: Two objects have the same mass; one moves faster. Which has more kinetic energy?

steps: More speed means more kinetic energy for the same mass.

items.prompt: Which has a bigger effect on kinetic energy, doubling mass or doubling speed?

steps: Kinetic energy depends on speed squared, so speed matters more.

items.prompt: A car doubles its speed. Does its kinetic energy exactly double?
items.answer: No, it increases about four times

steps: Kinetic energy depends on the speed squared.

items.prompt: Why does a fast-moving truck have a lot of kinetic energy?
items.answer: It has both large mass and high speed

steps: Large mass and high speed both raise kinetic energy.

items.prompt: A graph of kinetic energy versus speed rises steeply. What does this show?
items.answer: That kinetic energy increases sharply as speed increases

items.prompt: Does a parked car have kinetic energy? Explain.
items.answer: No, because it is not moving (speed is zero)

items.prompt: Why is a head-on crash at high speed more dangerous than at low speed?
items.answer: Higher speed means much more kinetic energy, so more energy is released in the crash

steps: Kinetic energy rises sharply with speed.
